seo.metaTitle: How to Set Up Phones to Record a Football Match
seo.metaDescription: Set up one or two phones to record football, reduce blind spots and choose the right fence mount, post mount or tripod for your pitch.

hero.h1: How to set up your phone to record a football match
hero.intro: Plan one-phone and two-phone football recording setups with safe mounting, consent, blind spots and venue rules in mind.

blocks.title: One-phone setup
blocks.description: Example central sideline camera position for a compact small-sided pitch.
notes: Use an elevated central position where venue rules allow.
Record a short test clip before kickoff.
Avoid unnecessary panning and digital zoom.
blocks.caption: Example only. Final placement depends on the pitch and safe mounting points.

blocks.title: Two-phone setup
blocks.description: Example opposing-halves setup for reducing blind spots on longer or wider small-sided pitches.
notes: Record an obvious synchronisation moment on both phones.
Keep orientation and settings consistent where possible.
blocks.caption: Example only. Two phones reduce blind spots, but they do not remove every obstruction.

blocks.title: Mount type by venue
blocks.disclosure: Some links may be affiliate links. Pitchside may earn a commission from qualifying purchases at no additional cost to you.

items.title: Budget fence mount
items.bestFor: Rigid fencing where the phone can be mounted safely outside the playing area.
items.limitations: Not suitable for loose netting or places where the phone could be struck by the ball.

items.title: Covered fence mount
items.bestFor: Outdoor venues where extra cover may help protect the phone from light weather exposure.
items.limitations: Does not remove the need for safe placement, venue permission or weather judgement.

items.title: Post mount
items.bestFor: Secure posts where venue rules allow mounting outside the playing area.
items.limitations: Check post stability and make sure the mount cannot fall into the pitch or pedestrian routes.
